scope: The positive-temperature, temperature-to-zero pair limit clause of cor:fsoft, with the excluded diagonal explicitly characterized. This review makes no SPNE or whole-network convergence claim.
semantic_findings: The filter is the right-hand neighborhood of zero, so the temperature approaches zero through positive values.
gate is the actual sigmoid of the score divided by temperature. Strictly positive and negative fixed scores tend to the corresponding infinities, yielding gate limits one and zero respectively.
softSplit is the actual pair (gate*u + temperature*binaryEntropy(gate), gate*v). Continuity of binary entropy on the closed interval, including its endpoints, makes the scaled entropy term vanish.

The two pair coordinates converge to the actual strict stopPair off the diagonal, with separate positive-score and negative-score cases. The proof is not restricted to a statement about their difference.
At a tied score the gate is exactly one half and the limit is (u/2,u/2). The theorem does not incorrectly extend strict-stopping pair convergence to nonzero tied inputs.
The statements accept arbitrary signed real inputs; the pairwise analytic limit needs no input positivity or gate differentiability premise.
